question.text: Conflict of interest management in an AIF requires:

answer.text: Detailed policies and procedures approved jointly by the Manager and Trustee, plus written policies to identify, monitor and mitigate conflicts of interest

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, Category I and II AIFs must have detailed policies and procedures approved jointly by the Manager and Trustee/Board to ensure fund decisions comply with regulations, PPM terms and investor agreements. Managers must additionally establish written policies and procedures to identify, monitor and mitigate conflicts of interest. The Trap: Disclosure alone is insufficient — the workbook requires active identification, monitoring and mitigation supported by written policies, not only annual-report disclosure. Note: Source-backed conflict-management elements include conflict disclosure, written policies, recusal, records of decisions, segregation of functions, and periodic review/update.
